newsitem.title: UK: Technically shaky gold nears key $350 level.
newsitem.headline: Technically shaky gold nears key $350 level.

text.p: Analysts painted a gloomy technical picture for gold on Wednesday after a new slide took prices down to a hair's breadth away from the psychological $350 an ounce level.
"It's a distinctly bearish picture. Gold has come under consistant selling pressure," said Elli Gifford, Investment Research of Cambridge.

Gold fixed in London on Wednesday morning at $352.45, lowest since October 4, 1993. In the immediate term the $350 area was likely to offer a modicum of support, analysts said, although more losses were seen in coming weeks towards $345, $341 and possibly $330.
Technical indicators are trending steeply lower, with 10- and 30-day moving averages currently at around $361 and $367.
The 14-day RSI is in oversold territory at around 20 percent, but that is no guarantee of a brisk corrective rally to come, analysts said.
Last week the RSI was even lower, yet the market was only able to muster a "dead cat bounce" capped at around $360.
"Even though it was very oversold and had a good reason to rally, it didn't," said Gifford.

Prices have declined some $15, or four percent, since the start of the yeart. Values tumbled $5 late Tuesday early Wednesday on fund selling and long liquidation, sparked by a surging dollar and fear of central bank gold sales.
Karen Jones of Credit Suisse First Boston noted that after breaking below $353.20 support, gold was now expected to challenge $350 and then $345.
Elliott Wave analysts put support slightly lower, adding that any corrective bounces would meet resistance around $355.
"Further losses below the psychological $350.00 would probably continue toward the September 1993 low at $341.00," analyst John Sowden of Elliott Wave International said in a commentary.

Eventually, prices may target $330, a key low level from the first half of 1993, analysts said. But pinpointing upcoming technical support levels is difficult because prices have not been so low in more than three years, some noted.
A ray of hope might shine if gold was able to clear $360 resistance, analysts said. But at the moment it did not appear able to muster the energy to do so.

"If the downtrend continues to accelerate, chances are it will bounce," said analyst Susan Rigg of Chart Analysis Ltd. "But gold will not be able to move higher unless it moves sideways for a period."
